coverage.title: Finite-horizon doubly robust off-policy value evaluation

Almost-additive sequences have a normalized limit

Exp4 expert reward estimates are conditionally unbiased
A finite MDP policy generates action-state-reward trajectories

Expected regret of explore-then-commit
Without trajectory coverage, logged data need not identify policy value
Finite-horizon simulation bound for one fixed policy

diagram_candidates.claim: The definition computes per-time target-policy values, cumulative action weights, and weighted TD residuals before averaging trajectory scores.
diagram_candidates.map_or_relations: Consider a finite-horizon trajectory strip s_0→a_0→r_1,s_1→… with per-step multiplier ρ_t, cumulative W_t=W_{t-1}ρ_t, residual r_{t+1}+γV_{t+1}−Q_t, discount γ^t, plus V_H=0 terminal condition and final n^{-1}ΣD_i. Keep model-fitting/training separation out of the path or label it clearly.

diagram_candidates.claim: Backward finite-horizon value recursion selects only the first action at s_0, which is executed in the true environment before replanning from the new state/model.
diagram_candidates.map_or_relations: A short horizon tree with model reward and transition branches feeding Q_h and V_h backward; highlight the returned first action, real transition/observation, and a separate re-invocation. Avoid implying the algorithm updates the model or guarantees true return.

diagram_candidates.claim: One episode is sampled with θ fixed at θ_0, then discounted returns and score vectors are summed to make a single post-episode parameter update.
diagram_candidates.map_or_relations: Timeline S_0,A_0,R_1,…,S_T with terminal stop; annotate G_t backward/discounted and ψ_t=∇logπ_{θ_0}; a single update θ_0→θ_1 only after episode completion. Distinguish γ^{k−t} inside returns from outer γ^t in update.

diagram_candidates.claim: Bregman divergence compares R(x) to the first-order tangent approximation at y, while the local primal/dual norms are induced by H_R(z) and its inverse.
diagram_candidates.map_or_relations: Optional 2D convex potential sketch showing point y, tangent plane/value at x, vertical gap B_R(x||y), and local Hessian metric pairing v with h. Mark as schematic; do not suggest Bregman divergence is symmetric or a metric.

diagram_candidates.claim: The Bellman residual δ_w is split into its projection onto the feature span V_μ and an orthogonal remainder; BE and PBE are the squared norms of the whole residual and projected component.
diagram_candidates.map_or_relations: Show V_μ as a subspace, δ_w decomposed as Π_μδ_w plus (I−Π_μ)δ_w perpendicular to V_μ; label PBE=||Πδ||² and BE=||δ||². Make explicit that geometry is in the μ-weighted quotient and zero-mass states are identified.

diagram_candidates.claim: At H=1 full support permits an unbiased action reweighting score, whereas behavior support omitting target action b leaves two reward models observationally indistinguishable.
diagram_candidates.map_or_relations: Two-panel one-step MDP: s_0 has actions a,b, both transition to z; panel 1 μ(a)=μ(b)=1/2 and π(b)=1, rewards r(a)=0,r(b)=1, weights 0/2; panel 2 μ(a)=1, π(b)=1 and branch b has reward +1 versus −1 in two observationally identical models. Distinguish support from transition coverage.

diagram_candidates.claim: Explore-then-commit samples each arm m times, then commits to arm 1; deterministic stacks make regret exactly mΔ while the theorem gives a larger upper bound.
diagram_candidates.map_or_relations: Timeline first 2m rounds split into m pulls per arm (round-robin if showing order), then n−2m arm-1 pulls; per-pull gaps 0 for arm 1 and Δ for arm 2; bracket the m arm-2 exploration pulls and show exact mΔ versus bound expression. Avoid suggesting every pull of arm 2 occurs consecutively.

diagram_candidates.claim: Finite trajectory-prefix probability factors at every time into policy action probability and joint next-state/reward kernel; marginalizing actions yields state-reward prefix probabilities.
diagram_candidates.map_or_relations: Time-indexed path S_n→A_n→(R_{n+1},S_{n+1}), with factor π(a_n|s_n)p(s_{n+1},r_{n+1}|s_n,a_n) per step; show action-sum at each time for marginal. Keep the joint order consistent with Z_n=(S_n,A_n,R_{n+1},S_{n+1}) and empty m=0 product.

diagram_candidates.claim: Behavior policy always logs action a with reward 0 in both processes, while target action b has reward +1 in M_+ and −1 in M_−; logged-data laws coincide but target-optimal actions differ.
diagram_candidates.map_or_relations: Paired one-step diagrams sharing s_0,z and logged edge a/0 to z; annotate behavior μ(a)=1 and target π(b)=1. Show unobserved b/ +1 in M_+ and b/−1 in M_−, then connect equal logged law to incompatible target values and optimal actions. Explicitly mark b unsupported under behavior.

Learner stochastic probability ε at g and expert choices are in prose and intentionally are not encoded as edge probabilities. No clipping/overlap defect.

MRP 2 shows A splitting equally to B/B′ with reward 0, B→A reward 1, and B′ splitting equally to B/B′ with reward −1. Diagram note correctly says B and B′ share features; visual labels are small but legible at original resolution. No clipping/overlap defect.
